page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-level virtual machine instance within the ecs.n1 server family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any bundled local storage or GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports AVX and AVX512F instruction sets, along with AES cryptography and BMI2, ADX, and FMA extensions.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.n1.medium in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.59 (bottom 25%) and a multi-core score of 2194.17 (bottom 10%). Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 959.0 and a multi-core score of 1698.0, both falling into the bottom 25% and 10% categories respectively. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 159.5 GB/sec and an uncached large block read bandwidth of 16.3 GB/sec. Database operations and web serving throughput are also limited, with Passmark database operations scoring 570.41 and static web serving throughput reaching 1.9 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but low-tier benchmark results, the ecs.n1.medium offers a basic entry point for workloads that require dedicated compute resources without high performance demands. The lack of local storage and low memory capacity make it unsuitable for data-intensive applications, large databases, or complex analytical tasks. It is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic web serving, simple background tasks, or development and testing environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded processing.
